subject: Energy
title: What Is Energy Poverty?
description: A quick, practical guide to What Is Energy Poverty?.

hook.text: About 750 million people have no electricity—and 2.3 billion still cook with wood, charcoal, or dung indoors.

buildup.text: Energy poverty means lacking access to modern energy services—clean cooking, reliable lighting, and basic appliances.

discovery.text: Indoor air pollution from cooking fires kills 3.2 million people yearly—mostly women and children in poorer nations.

twist.text: Sub-Saharan Africa uses less electricity per capita than a single US refrigerator consumes—an extreme inequality.

climax.text: Universal energy access is SDG 7—the UN target to provide affordable, reliable, modern energy for all by 2030.

punchline.text: Billions lack basic power—energy poverty is the silent crisis.

quiz.question: How many people still lack electricity globally?
